rv.q: Motown The Musical comes across as a muddled vanity exercise by Mr Gordy, still going strong at 86, and here credited as lead producer and librettist.
Like the legendary music catalog from Motown, the revival that re-opened Thursday night at the Nederlander Theatre is alternately catchy and soulful, and overstuffed with memorable melodies.
Unfortunately, whatever gift the legendary Motown founder has for discovering talent, he lacks in storytelling.
But who’s coming to see “Motown” for anything other than the fabulous songbook?
And while Gordy's script may be an awkward ball of confusion, to cite a late Temptations hit, you might not be able to help yourself (sugar pie, honey bunch) from having a just good enough time.

If you can ignore the cringe-inducing book scenes, you will probably have a good time at Motown, especially if you're the kind of person who can't listen to a whole song on your iPod without hitting skip.
This time around, I didn’t fall.
Still, this elaborate, very busy production ought to please anyone looking to take a nostalgia trip and overlook its problems.

"It plays as an entirely different, and noticeably less compelling, show than the original version that ran on Broadway...This is not to say I was an enormous fan of that incarnation—I wasn't—but it had a size, energy, and (relative) intensity that this one lacks...It's imparted a jagged choppiness that keeps the evening from cohering...
Among the best things I've ever seen on a stage.
From the opening notes of the first song, the audience is clapping, moving in their seats, and struggling – sometimes unsuccessfully –
But if the book disappoints, the dynamic company is well worth catching.
